tools.name: reticle
tools.description: Reticle harness tools

tools.name: glob_files
tools.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

tools.name: outline
tools.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

tools.name: search_text
tools.description: Search case-sensitive literal text by default, or Python regex with regex=true. Returns one line per matching line as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers; context_lines adds surrounding lines. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. Literal text, or a Python pattern when regex=true.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

tools.name: replace_text
tools.description: Replace literal text in a file, treating LF and CRLF line endings as equivalent. Preserve existing bytes outside the replacement and use local line endings for new_text. Other whitespace must match exactly. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description: Apply a single-file unified diff to an existing file. Exact line positions and context must match; all hunks are validated before writing. LF/CRLF differences are tolerated and local endings preserved. Supply path and patch (optional ---/+++ headers followed by @@ hunks). Use write_file to create files.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

tools.name: read_output
tools.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

tools.name: search_output
tools.description: Search an earlier output for literal text or optional Python regex, with surrounding context.

tools.name: finish
tools.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

tools.name: verify
tools.description: Run the fixed project tests. Full results are returned; this tool is available in all conditions.

tools.name: glob_files
tools.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

tools.name: outline
tools.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

tools.name: search_text
tools.description: Search case-sensitive literal text by default, or Python regex with regex=true. Returns one line per matching line as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers; context_lines adds surrounding lines. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. Literal text, or a Python pattern when regex=true.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

tools.name: replace_text
tools.description: Replace literal text in a file, treating LF and CRLF line endings as equivalent. Preserve existing bytes outside the replacement and use local line endings for new_text. Other whitespace must match exactly. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description: Apply a single-file unified diff to an existing file. Exact line positions and context must match; all hunks are validated before writing. LF/CRLF differences are tolerated and local endings preserved. Supply path and patch (optional ---/+++ headers followed by @@ hunks). Use write_file to create files.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

tools.name: read_output
tools.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

tools.name: search_output
tools.description: Search an earlier output for literal text or optional Python regex, with surrounding context.

tools.name: finish
tools.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.
